title: Attention TNA
text: Regular TNA looks pairs states happen one right . student Plan time 3 Monitor time 4, TNA counts transition. ignores relationship Plan time 3 Adapt time 7. two events four steps apart, TNA treats unrelated. problem earlier events still matter later . student plans start session still influenced planning adapt several steps later. user’s first prompt chatbot conversation shapes responses several turns line. cases, connection two events real — ’s just immediate. ATNA fills gap. Instead counting adjacent transitions, looks pairs states across whole sequence weights far apart . Close events get high weight. Distant events get low weight. weight drops following exponential curve, nearby things matter lot far-away things matter little — still matter.

title: Attention TNA
text: Take sequence student actions: Regular TNA draws line pair neighbors: Plan→Monitor, Monitor→Discuss, Discuss→Emotion, . Seven events produce six edges. ATNA draws lines every pair, decreasing weight: Plan→Monitor (1 step apart): strong connection Plan→Discuss (2 steps apart): weaker Plan→Emotion (3 steps apart): weaker still Plan→Adapt (4 steps apart): faint Plan→Monitor (5 steps apart): faint Plan→Plan (6 steps apart): barely starting every event sequence. weighted connections get added across every sequence data. result weight matrix cell captures often state appears state B, weighted close together tend .
code: Plan → Monitor → Discuss → Emotion → Adapt → Monitor → Plan

text: Permutation tests edge weight centrality differences.  also accepts group tna model object.
code: permutation_test(x, y, adjust = "none", iter = 1000, paired = FALSE,                  level = 0.05, measures = character(0), ...) model_x <- tna(group_regulation[1:200, ]) model_y <- tna(group_regulation[1001:1200, ]) perm <- permutation_test(model_x, model_y, iter = 100) print(perm) #> # A tibble: 81 × 4 #>    edge_name           diff_true effect_size p_value #>    <chr>                   <dbl>       <dbl>   <dbl> #>  1 adapt -> adapt       0             NA     1       #>  2 cohesion -> adapt    0.00541        0.949 0.802   #>  3 consensus -> adapt  -0.000679      -0.175 0.752   #>  4 coregulate -> adapt  0.00769        0.568 0.624   #>  5 discuss -> adapt    -0.130         -7.11  0.00990 #>  6 emotion -> adapt     0.0101         1.59  0.257   #>  7 monitor -> adapt    -0.00480       -0.367 0.970   #>  8 plan -> adapt        0.00339        1.56  0.0297  #>  9 synthesis -> adapt  -0.159         -2.08  0.0594  #> 10 adapt -> cohesion   -0.0907        -1.23  0.238   #> # ℹ 71 more rows plot(perm) permg <- permutation_test(gmodel, iter = 100)

title: Transition Network Analysis (TNA)
text: tna R package analysis relational dynamics Transition Network Analysis (TNA). TNA provides tools building TNA models, plotting transition networks, calculating centrality measures, identifying dominant events patterns. TNA statistical techniques (e.g., bootstrapping permutation tests) ensure reliability observed insights confirm identified dynamics meaningful. See (Saqr et al., 2025) details TNA.

code: library("tna") data("group_regulation", package = "tna") tna_model <- tna(group_regulation) summary(tna_model) plot(tna_model) cent <- centralities(tna_model) plot(cent, ncol = 3) estimate_centrality_stability(tna_model) #> Centrality Stability Coefficients #>  #>  InStrength OutStrength Betweenness  #>         0.9         0.9         0.9 coms <- communities(tna_model) plot(coms) cqs <- cliques(tna_model, threshold = 0.12) plot(cqs) tna_model_start_high <- tna(group_regulation[1:1000, ]) tna_model_start_low <- tna(group_regulation[1001:2000, ]) comparison <- permutation_test(   tna_model_start_high,    tna_model_start_low,   measures = c("InStrength") ) plot_compare(tna_model_start_high, tna_model_start_low) plot(comparison) print(comparison$centralities$stats)

title: Bootstrap Transition Networks from Sequence Data — bootstrap
text: x tna group_tna object created sequence data. Grouped models scaled edge weights, networks, resampled (error class tna_error_scaling). iter integer specifying number bootstrap samples draw. Defaults 1000. level numeric value representing significance level hypothesis testing confidence intervals. Defaults 0.05. method character string. argument defines bootstrap test statistic. "stability" option (default) compares edge weights range "consistent" values defined consistency_range. Weights fall outside range considered insignificant. words, edge considered significant value within range (1 - level) * 100% bootstrap samples. "threshold" option instead compares edge weights user-specified threshold value. threshold numeric value compare edge weights . default 10th percentile edge weights. Used method = "threshold". consistency_range numeric vector length 2. Determines much edge weights may deviate (multiplicatively) observed values () considered insignificant. default c(0.75, 1.25) corresponds symmetric 25% deviation range. Used method = "stability". seed single numeric random seed reproducible resampling, NULL (default) use current RNG state. actor optional actor identifier sequences nested actors (example, several sessions per student). Either character string naming non-sequence column data model built (column meta_data prepare_data()), vector one identifier per sequence (per sequence data grouped model built , group_tna object). given, whole actors resampled replacement instead single sequences (cluster bootstrap; Davison & Hinkley, 1997, Section 3.8), sequences nested actors treated independent. default NULL resamples sequences.

title: Build a Transition Network Analysis Model — build_model
text: x stslist (TraMineR), data.frame, matrix, tna_data object (see prepare_data()). stslist data.frame objects x describe sequence events states used building Markov model.  x matrix, assumed element row column j weight edge representing transition state state j. x data.frame, must wide format (see cols define columns time points). ... Ignored. build_model aliases (e.g., tna), argument matches actual arguments build_model beside x. type character string describing weight matrix type. Currently supports following types: "relative" relative frequencies (probabilities, default) "frequency" frequencies. "co-occurrence" co-occurrences. "n-gram" n-gram transitions. Captures higher-order transitions considering sequences n states, useful identifying longer patterns. "gap" allows transitions non-adjacent states, transitions weighted gap size. "reverse" considers sequences reverse order (resulting called reply network contexts). resulting weight matrix transpose "frequency" option. "attention" aggregates downstream pairs states exponential decay gap states. parameter lambda can used control decay rate (default 1)- scaling character vector describing scale weights defined type. vector provided, scaling options applied respective order. example, c("rank", "minmax") first compute ranks, scale unit interval using min-max normalization. empty vector corresponds scaling. Currently supports following options: "minmax" performs min-max normalization scale weights unit interval. Note smallest weight positive, zero scaling. "max" Multiplies weights reciprocal largest weight scale weights unit interval. options preserves positive ranks, unlike "minmax" weights positive. "rank" Computes ranks weights using base::rank() ties.method = "average". params list additional arguments models specific type. potential elements list : n_gram: integer n-gram transitions specifying number adjacent events. default value 2. max_gap: integer gap-allowed transitions specifying largest allowed gap size. default 1. windowed: Perform model estimation window. Supported relative, frequency co-occurrence types. window_size: integer sliding window transitions specifying window size. default 2. window_type: character string defines window type. Either "rolling" "tumbling". weighted: logical value. TRUE, transitions weighted inverse sequence length. Can used frequency, co-occurrence reverse model types. default FALSE. direction: character string specifying direction attention models type = "attention". available options "backward", "forward", "", backward attention, forward attention, bidirectional attention, respectively. default "forward". decay: function specifies decay weights two time points specific distance. function take three arguments: , j lambda, j numeric vectors time values, lambda  numeric value decay rate. function return numeric vector weights. default function(, j, lambda) exp(-abs(- j) / lambda). lambda: numeric value decay rate. default 1. time: matrix data.frame providing time values sequence time index. tna_data objects, can also logical value, TRUE use time_data element x time values. Date values converted numeric. duration: matrix data.frame providing time spent state sequence time index. alternative time. inits optional numeric vector initial state probabilities state. vector scaled unity. cols expression giving tidy selection columns considered sequence data. default, columns used. concat integer number consecutive sequences concatenate. default 1 (concatenation). begin_state character string additional begin state. state added first observation every sequence signify beginning sequence end_state character string additional end state. state added last observation every sequence signify end sequence.

title: Calculate Centrality Measures for a Transition Matrix — centralities
text: following measures provided: OutStrength: Outgoing strength centrality, calculated using igraph::strength() mode = "". measures total weight outgoing edges node. InStrength: Incoming strength centrality, calculated using igraph::strength() mode = "". measures total weight incoming edges node. ClosenessIn: Closeness centrality (incoming), calculated using igraph::closeness() mode = "". measures close node nodes based incoming paths. ClosenessOut: Closeness centrality (outgoing), calculated using igraph::closeness() mode = "". measures close node nodes based outgoing paths. Closeness: Closeness centrality (overall), calculated using igraph::closeness() mode = "". measures close node nodes based incoming outgoing paths. Betweenness: Betweenness centrality defined number geodesics calculated using igraph::betweenness(). BetweennessRSP: Betweenness centrality based randomized shortest paths (Kivimäki et al. 2016). measures extent node lies shortest paths nodes. Diffusion: Diffusion centrality Banerjee et.al. (2014). measures influence node spreading information network. Diffusion always min-max normalized range 0 1, whatever value normalize, raw values grow powers edge weights (frequency model easily exceed 1e30). raw values equal every state, example relative transition network loops = TRUE every row sums one, normalized values NaN: measure distinguish states. Clustering: Signed clustering coefficient Zhang Horvath (2005) based symmetric adjacency matrix (sum adjacency matrix transpose). measures degree nodes tend cluster together. PageRank: Weighted PageRank centrality calculated using igraph::page_rank() directed transition network.

title: Test the Markov Order of Sequence Data — markov_order
text: order \(k = 1, \ldots,\) max_order, test compares order \(k - 1\) (null hypothesis) order \(k\). Every window \(k + 1\) consecutive states split context \(w\) (\(k - 1\) states next state), state \(x\) order \(k\) adds (\(k\) steps back), next state \(s\). null hypothesis, \(s\) independent \(x\) given \(w\). tested likelihood-ratio statistic $$G^2 = 2 \sum_{w, x, s} N_{wxs}   \log \frac{N_{wxs} N_{w}}{N_{wx} N_{ws}}$$ \(\sum_w (r_w - 1)(c_w - 1)\) degrees freedom, \(r_w\) \(c_w\) numbers distinct states \(x\) \(s\) observed context \(w\) (Anderson & Goodman, 1957). \(k = 1\) context empty, test whether next state depends current state . p-value comes conditional permutation test: within context \(w\), next states shuffled, keeps every count null hypothesis conditions . windows sequence overlap, permutation distribution approximates null distribution exact (exact test sample whole sequences counts; Besag & Mondal, 2013). asymptotic \(\chi^2\) p-value reported alongside. orders tested sequence: order raised test rejects level level. selected order highest order whose test, test every lower order, rejected. Order 0 means next state depend current state, max_order means test failed reject. results also contain log-likelihood, AIC, BIC multi-order model order (Scholtes, 2017). model uses state frequencies first state sequence highest available order following state. dof = "paths", parameters order transitions paths first-order transitions allow, observed (Scholtes, 2017). dof = "observed", transitions observed data counted. orders minimize AIC BIC reported next selected order, affect test. tests stop first order reject, dependence skips order (example, state two steps back current state) selected. warning class tna_warning_markov_order therefore raised, note printed, test order selected order plus one rejects, AIC BIC select different order tests. class warning raised iter small p-value fall level (fewer floor(1 / level) permutations). Sequences split missing values, window spans missing value, parts fewer two states used. windows treated independent observations, sequences nested actors (example, several sessions per student) taken account.

title: Compute User Sessions from Event Data — prepare_data
text: data data.frame containing action/event data. actor character vector expression represents tidy selection names columns represent user/actor identifiers. provided neither time order specified, entire dataset treated single session. case multiple actors, readable .actor column added grouping uses original columns keep distinct combinations separate. time character string expression giving name column representing timestamps action events. action character string expression giving name column holding information action taken. order character string expression giving name column sequence numbers non-unique orderable values indicate order within actor group, present ordered data actor available, used widening data. actor time specified, sequence order specified determines order events within actor session. time_threshold positive numeric value specifying time threshold seconds creating new time-based sessions. Set FALSE disable gap-based session splitting, actor-session combination forms one session. Defaults 900 seconds. custom_format character string giving format used parse time column. is_unix_time logical value indicating whether time column Unix time. default FALSE. unix_time_unit character string giving Unix time unit is_unix_time TRUE. default "seconds". Valid options "seconds", "milliseconds", "microseconds". unused_fn handle extra columns pivoting wide format. See tidyr::pivot_wider(). default keep columns use first value. timezone Olson time zone used interpret timestamps contain explicit UTC offset. Explicit offsets Z, +00:00, -0500 always honored. default "UTC" reproducible results across systems. See OlsonNames(). session optional tidy selection one columns identifying explicit sessions within actors, course semester. time also supplied, actor-session combination can split time_threshold.

title: Compute User Sessions from Event Data — prepare_data
text: tna_data object, list following elements: long_data: processed data long format. sequence_data: processed data sequences wide format, actions/events different variables structured sequences. meta_data: variables original data wide format. time_data: Parsed timestamps wide format time supplied, NULL otherwise. statistics: list containing summary statistics: total sessions, total actions, unique users, time range (applicable), top sessions user activities.

title: Build a Random Group Transition Network Analysis Model — random_group_tna
text: n_groups integer giving number groups. NULL (default), value drawn 2:4 call. group_names optional character vector group names length n_groups. Defaults "Group 1", "Group 2", ... n_states integer >= 2 giving number states. NULL (default), value drawn 7:11 call. states optional character vector state labels length least n_states. first n_states used. NULL (default), labels taken category auto-picked built-pool fits n_states. category optional character string naming built-label pool. Available pools returned list_random_state_pools(). NULL (default), pool whose size least n_states sampled random. Ignored states supplied. alpha positive numeric Dirichlet concentration parameter. Small values (e.g. 0.3) produce sparse, peaked transitions; large values (e.g. 5) produce near-uniform transitions. NULL (default), value drawn Uniform(0.5, 1.0) call. diag_boost non-negative numeric added diagonal transition matrix re-normalising rows. Larger values make states "stickier" (self-transitions). NULL (default), value drawn Uniform(1.5, 3.0) call. n_sequences integer giving number sequences simulate true parameters. NULL (default), value drawn 500:800 call. seq_length integer giving length simulated sequence. NULL (default), value drawn 6:20 call. type character string giving model type. One "relative" (default), "frequency", "co-occurrence", "attention". per_group optional list length n_groups. element list overrides applied group . Recognised override names: alpha, diag_boost, trans_matrix, init_probs, n_sequences, seq_length. Unset entries fall back top-level defaults (may drawn random NULL). seed integer random seed reproducibility, NULL (default) fresh randomness every call.

text: Fixed case-insensitive argument matching preserve canonical option names, allowing cluster_data() cluster_sequences() pass "ward.D" "ward.D2" correctly stats::hclust(). Disabled time splitting now bypasses gap computation keeps missing-time events actor-session sequence. Documented time_data component returned prepare_data(). prune() now warns inactive method-specific arguments treats supplied bootstrap object request bootstrap pruning. Added reproducible seed arguments network clique bootstrapping. Added weighted PageRank centralities(). plot.tna_permutation() now dispatches dedicated permutation renderer cograph::splot(), permutation-specific options show_nonsig, show_stars, show_effect, edge_nonsig_color, edge_nonsig_style, edge_nonsig_alpha honored.
